Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has tweaked the front wing’s shape and end‑plates to smooth out how the airflow hits it, giving the car a more stable front end and better grip through the corners. On the rear, they’ve reshaped the top wing tip for this circuit to fine‑tune the balance between downforce and straight‑line speed, helping the car stay glued to the track while still being quick on the straights. These changes should translate into more confidence in turn‑in and a stronger overall pace for the weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has re‑shaped the first two sections of the front wing, tweaking the little flaps and tips that sit on them. The goal is to give the car a more consistent bite up front, which translates into better grip and stability through the high‑speed corners this weekend. In short, the car should feel more planted and easier to drive, especially when pushing hard into the bends.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has added a bigger, more complex wing on the floor edge and reshaped the small fence that guides air under the car, giving the chassis extra downforce and a more stable front end. The rear wing has also been tweaked, with a new profile on both the main element and its flap, tightening the car’s rear grip. Together, these changes should improve cornering stability and tyre wear, giving the team a better chance to fight for podium positions this weekend.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin’s latest fix to the front wing reshapes the tiny tip between the wing elements and its end‑plate, while also tweaking the main sections to meet the new TD018H rule. The result is a cleaner, more consistent airflow up front, giving the car a bit more bite and stability when it’s on the edge of a corner. In short, the update should let the drivers extract a little extra grip and confidence during this weekend’s sprint and main race.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has tweaked the shape of the floor’s edge panels and the surrounding bodywork, essentially reshaping the “fences” that channel airflow under the car. The new profile should smooth the air flow, giving a modest boost in down‑force and reducing drag, which translates into better grip in corners and a little extra straight‑line speed—exactly what the team needs to be more competitive this weekend.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has tweaked the front‑wing’s mechanical setup, tightening the flap angles to give a little extra front‑end grip without adding too much drag. The change should make the car turn into corners more confidently and help the drivers keep a steadier line through the slower sections of the circuit. In short, it’s a modest aero tweak aimed at improving balance and tyre wear for this weekend’s race.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has refreshed the front wing, endplates and nose, giving the car a cleaner, more consistent airflow up front. The new lower‑center wing section and tweaked wing‑tip connections shave a little drag while keeping the front end stable, and the reshaped nose lifts the underside and drops the tip to improve grip into the corners. In plain terms, the car should feel more planted on the straights and turn‑in sharper for this weekend’s layout.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams have tweaked the front wing to meet the new deflection rules, giving the rear‑wing flap a slightly flatter shape and adjusting the end‑plate angle for smoother airflow. The same geometric tweaks have been carried over to the rear‑corner package and cooling louvers, helping the car stay cooler and more stable on the track. In short, these changes should keep the car balanced and keep the tyres in the right temperature window for the weekend’s sprint.

Sauber / Audi.summary: Sauber‑Audi’s new floor package – a reshaped floor fence, tweaked edge and a refined diffuser – is aimed at giving the car a steadier rear and more consistent down‑force, especially through the fast corners. A lighter‑looking engine cover tweaks the airflow over the top of the car, helping the aero balance stay smoother as the fuel load drops. Finally, a subtle reshaping of the front‑wing’s main‑plane to end‑plate transition should clean up the front end, giving the drivers a bit more bite out of the corners this weekend.
